spec_match.rationale: Implements the streaming-export motivation: chunk to int16 PCM to growing WAV, with playback and download of the genuinely produced file.

interactive.rationale: Run button drives render+encode with a native progress bar, waveform, path banner, playback via AudioContext, and a Blob download link.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Blurb promises the end-to-end export with path labelling; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Classic-path fallback is labelled (never claimed incremental); decode failure and render failure branches surface real errors; WAV size is asserted against 44+frames*2.

references.rationale: Links chromestatus.com/feature/<id> plus the exact spec anchor in see-also.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite applies; injected panel executed here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified on headless Chromium 141 (predates Chrome 158, feature absent even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features) via Playwright 1.56 at desktop 1280x800 and mobile 360x740 DPR3 touch, driving every control; screenshots under /tmp/claude-0/agentB/shots/. Export completed (88200 frames to a ~172 KB WAV), path banner correctly read classic one-shot, playback decoded and played 4.00s from the Blob, download link appeared.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry.assert covers the primary contract and the explicit fallback branch; console output is intentional and prefixed.

design_system.rationale: Only CSS variables from public/styles.css; buttons overriding background also set color; AA pairs (text-charcoal/bg-stone, bg-ivory/text-black, accent-emerald-dark on paper).

accessibility.rationale: Native controls with labels, visible focus (verified first-Tab), caption+scope tables, aria-live polite result regions.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Both viewports clean; action row wraps; download link is a 44px bordered target.

openQuestions.title: Re-verify the supported path on a real Chrome 158 / Canary build
openQuestions.detail: This environment's Chromium 141 lacks the surface even behind --enable-experimental-web-platform-features, so only the honest-absent branch ran. On Chrome 158 (or Canary with the feature's runtime flag) verify: the incremental path banner: >1 pulls with only one chunk of float data in flight while the same WAV is produced.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Represent task completion with a real progress element styled to the design system.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native <progress max value> with an accessible name plus a text readout of frames rendered; updated per chunk.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Expose canvas content to assistive tech, e.g. via HTML-in-canvas (layoutsubtree).
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Exception recorded: layoutsubtree/HTML-in-canvas is itself experimental and unavailable on the verification build, so the guidance's fallback strategy is used instead - canvas has role=img with aria-labelledby/aria-describedby and a text equivalent (frame count, duration, peak amplitude) updated on every draw.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Landmarks, native semantics, accessible names, visible focus, and polite live regions for asynchronous state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Content sits in main/header/footer landmarks; async results land in aria-live=polite output/status elements; tables carry caption plus th scope=col; first-Tab focus visibility verified in the browser.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsically-sized grid/flex layouts (auto-fit + minmax) so panels reflow without horizontal overflow at narrow widths.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Control panels use grid-template-columns repeat(auto-fit, minmax()), tables are wrapped in overflow-x containers, and long tokens use overflow-wrap: anywhere; verified no horizontal overflow at 360px.

summary: A real file out of a real render on every build, with the path that produced it named truthfully.
